answer: Challenge-Derived Microtask Seeding. Each identity must solve a freshly generated microtask whose answer depends on a hidden seed drawn from a public meadow of task templates, with the mapping held by a rotating issuer. Correct answers release a marble-sized credential, but the seed rotates per applicant, so a copied answer fails against the next kernel. An attacker must run live computation and human judgment per identity rather than replaying captured answers, paying full marginal cost every time.
